The purple worm can violently regurgitate a creature or boulder it has swallowed to make a ranged Strike. The Strike deals bludgeoning damage depending on the size of the projectile:

  • Tiny @Damage[(2d6+13)[bludgeoning]]{2d6+13}
  • Small @Damage[(3d6+13)[bludgeoning]]{3d6+13}
  • Medium @Damage[(4d6+13)[bludgeoning]]{4d6+13}
  • Large @Damage[(5d6+13)[bludgeoning]]{5d6+13}
  • Huge @Damage[(6d6+13)[bludgeoning]]{6d6+13}

A regurgitated creature takes falling damage from the height of the target or from 20 feet, whichever is greater.

Boulders occupy space in the worm's stomach as a creature of equivalent size, and purple worms often have several boulders swallowed. A purple worm can use a single action to swallow a new boulder.

The ongoing effect of investigating the machinations of Nhimbaloth and her servants moves from the realm of sleep to your waking moments. Ominous cracks in the fabric of reality appear before your eyes, fraying the edges of your sanity. You are no longer certain of who your friends are. Allies appear to shed their disguises and reveal themselves to be malevolent monsters.

path: Murmur, The Implement of Empty Death
items.en:
When an occult spellcaster of the Empty Death seeks to give any type of regenerative ability to a particularly powerful and resource-intensive void creation (an ongoing spell, a complex hazard, or even a creature), they sometimes elect to use a separate implement to achieve this end. This implement draws void energy from the River of Souls, where the Empty Death hunts, funneling and amplifying that energy to a specific place on the mortal plane. The void energy can then be used to power the spellcaster's creation (or creations). While an object imbued with occult power makes for an adequate implement, a living creature used in this way generates a purer form of void energy as well as more consistent output. However, most beings, even those with no conscience, will refuse to use a living creature for such experiments, knowing that to do so would be to condemn that creature to an eternal life of unimaginable pain.

Unfortunately, those who serve the Empty Death — an inscrutable, malevolent Elder God with neither edicts nor anathemas — have no such scruples. These spellcasters are perfectly willing to capture and enslave a sentient creature to achieve their macabre goals. Many even take obscene delight in the process, which, among other things, involves permanently inflicting the feeblemind condition on the creature to domesticate and control it, scraping every ounce of soul energy from its mortal shell, and cruelly reshaping that soul energy to withstand the continual agony of serving as a living void energy source. Through a final series of unspeakable experiments, the spellcaster then consigns part of the creature's soul essence to the River of Souls while imprisoning the other part of the soul to a specific location on the material plane. The resulting abomination is known as an implement of the Empty Death, a tortured soul used as a living conduit between the Empty Death's plane and the mortal realm.

Sometimes known as a pale thrall, an implement of the Empty Death lives a life of perpetual, horrendous torment, possessing barely a spark of intelligence beyond the level of an average, nonmagical animal. At times, the implement's former life returns to them in vague, fragmented flashes of memory, but they can do nothing with these images. Indeed, they are incapable of speech beyond the simplest of words, which frequently takes the form of a plea to be killed and thereby released from their eternal suffering.

Implements of the Empty Death typically retain most or all of the abilities they had before their enslavement, though their creators will sometimes modify, augment, or add abilities to help the implement defend itself.

If there are no creatures within its Petrifying Gaze aura at the start of its turn, the haunt spends 1 action to emit a shrill scream that alerts its creator to the presence of intruders. It then uses an action to shut and lock the door and resets.

Disabling this haunt permanently destroys it, and the imprisoned creature dies.

The haunt fixes their glare at a creature they can see within 30 feet. The target must immediately attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:30] save against the haunt's petrifying gaze. The haunt's gaze is unaffected by walls or other nonmagical barriers.

If the creature was already slowed by petrifying gaze before attempting its save, a failed save causes it to be petrified permanently. After attempting its save, the creature is then temporarily immune until the start of the haunt's next turn.

Slavers and raiders from the cold, windswept dimension of Leng, these malevolent humanoids range across reality in ominous black ships capable of sailing beyond the borders of dimensions and planes. Although most denizens of Leng seek slaves and plunder like any pirate, others operate as self-styled ambassadors and merchants, sowing discord with far-ranging plots. While the inscrutable denizens dress themselves in flowing robes, veils, and broad turbans to appear human, their aberrant physiology, when glimpsed, is evident from their crown of stubby horns and tentacled jaws to their furry, goat-like legs.

Above the fierce captains who command the infamous black ships are an even higher caste of denizens of Leng. These cultists and musicians serve as high priests, laboring to appease the frightening gods who look down upon the Nightmare Realm with cold malice.
Male denizen of leng
planar fast healing 10

The target can understand all words regardless of language and also speak the languages of other creatures. When in a mixed group of creatures, each time the target speaks, it can choose a creature and speak in a language that creature understands, even if the target doesn't know what language that is.

Heightened (7th) The duration is 8 hours.

A denizen of Leng maintains a connection to Leng at all times, and when away from Leng, they have fast healing 5. They lose this ability on Leng or in areas where planar connections do not function. If killed, their body dissolves into nothingness in [[/br 1d4 #Dissolve Body]]{1d4 rounds}, leaving behind their equipment. A slain denizen reforms in Leng; they can be permanently killed only when their planar fast healing doesn't function.

@Localize[PF2E.NPC.Abilities.Glossary.FastHealing]
Denizens of Leng don't need to breathe.

A creature that takes damage from a denizen's bite must succeed at a @Check[type:fortitude|dc:27] save or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1}. Each time a target fails an additional save against this ability, the condition value increases by 1 (to a maximum of Clumsy 4). This condition value decreases by 1 every 24 hours.

Many denizens of Leng carry strange rubies mined from quarries in Leng. As long as a creature holds a Leng ruby that it willingly accepted as a gift or payment from a denizen of Leng, any denizen of Leng can target that creature with @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.KSAEhNfZyXMO7Z7V]{Outcast's Curse}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.R8bqnYiThB6MYTxD]{Phantom Pain}, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.KHnhPHL4x1AQHfbC]{Mind Reading} at a range of 1 mile, and the bearer uses an outcome one degree of success worse than the result of its saving throw against Outcast's Curse.

You create a sphere of altered gravity. All creatures and unsecured objects in the area move towards the center, depending on their Reflex saving throws. This follows the rules for forced movement. If there's not enough space near the center of the sphere, creatures and objects nearer to the center move first, and others move as far as they can without being blocked, up to the amount set by their saving throw outcomes.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature moves 5 feet toward the center.

Failure The creature moves 15 feet toward the center.

Critical Failure The creature moves 30 feet toward the center.

Illusions bend light around the target, rendering it @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.zJxUflt9np0q4yML]{Invisible}. This makes it @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VRSef5y1LmL2Hkjf]{Undetected} to all creatures, though the creatures can attempt to find the target, making it @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.iU0fEDdBp3rXpTMC]{Hidden} to them instead. If the target uses a hostile action, the spell ends after that hostile action is completed.

Heightened (4th) The spell lasts 1 minute, but it doesn't end if the target uses a hostile action.

You whisper baleful secrets that transcend language and carry magically to the ears of your foes. The words take physical form, weakening the life force of the targets, each of which must attempt a Fortitude save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature takes @Damage[(floor(@item.rank/2))d8[persistent,void]] damage.

Failure The creature takes @Damage[(floor(@item.rank/2)*2)d8[persistent,void]] damage and becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 1}.

Critical Failure The creature takes @Damage[(floor(@item.rank/2)*2)d8[persistent,void]] damage and becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 2} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.3uh1r86TzbQvosxv]{Doomed 1}.

Heightened (+2) The persistent void damage increases by 1d8 on a success, or by 2d8 on a failure or critical failure.

Misshapen skeletal forms erupt from a solid surface, such as a stone floor, and fill the burst. The area they fill is difficult terrain. Their grasping claws deal 2d6 slashing damage to creatures on the ground in the area when the skeletons first appear with a basic Reflex save.

On subsequent rounds, the first time you Sustain the Spell each round, you can move the area of skeletons up to 20 feet within the range of the spell and deal 2d6 slashing damage with a basic Reflex save to each creature in the new area.

Damaging or destroying the skeletons is irrelevant, as new bones pull forth from the ground to repair and replace any that are obliterated.

Heightened (+2) The damage increases by 1d6.

As long as he exerts full control over Dorianna, Ysondkhelir gains the following abilities:

  • He is Huge, instead of his normal size, with a reach of 15 feet on melee attacks.

  • He has damage resistance 10 (physical).

  • He gains the Spawn Hand action.

  • He is Quickened. He can only use the extra action granted by the Quickened condition to Cast a Spell or to Spawn Hand.

As long as Ysondkhelir is alive, any square of his dreamworld that lacks a solid floor is considered to be a nightmare space. A character who enters or ends their turn in a nightmare space triggers the effect below, as the dream-catcher's malevolent nightmares tear into their mind.

@Check[type:will|dc:26|showDC:all]{basic Will save}

@Damage[(2d10+13)[spirit,mental]]{2d10+13 spirit and mental damage}

Critical success No damage. The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1}.

Success Half damage. The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 2}.

Failure Full damage. The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 3}.

Critical failure Double damage. The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 4}.
Ysondkhelir spawns a giant crawling hand in an unoccupied space within 30 feet.

You raise a magical shield of force. This counts as using the Raise a Shield action, giving you a +1 circumstance bonus to AC until the start of your next turn, but it doesn't require a hand to use.

While the spell is in effect, you can use the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.feats-srd.Item.jM72TjJ965jocBV8]{Shield Block} reaction with your magic shield. The shield has Hardness 5. You can use the spell's reaction to reduce damage from any spell or magical effect, even if it doesn't deal physical damage. After you use Shield Block, the spell ends and you can't cast it again for 10 minutes.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.Jemq5UknGdMO7b73]{Spell Effect: Shield}

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.QF6RDlCoTvkVHRo4]{Effect: Shield Immunity}

Heightened (+2) The shield's Hardness increases by 5.

You hurl a loose, unattended object that is within range and that has 1 Bulk or less at the target. Make a spell attack roll against the target. If you hit, you deal 2d6 bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage—as appropriate for the object you hurled. No specific traits or magic properties of the hurled item affect the attack or the damage.

Critical Success You deal double damage.

Success You deal full damage.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d6.

A mass of snakes made of shadow rise up to capture creatures in the area. Each creature in the area when you Cast the Spell takes @Damage[3d6[piercing]] damage and @Damage[1d6[persistent,poison]] damage from a biting snake, and it's @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained} depending on its Reflex save. A creature that ends its turn in the area must also attempt this save, even if it's already grabbed or restrained by the snakes. You can Dismiss the spell.

Success The creature is unaffected.

Failure The creature takes full damage and is grabbed by a snake. The snakes' @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.SkZAQRkLLkmBQNB9]{Escape} DC is equal to your spell DC. A creature can attack a snake to release the creature. A snake's AC is equal to your spell DC, and it's destroyed if it takes 12 or more damage at once. New snakes continually regrow as long as the spell lasts, so destroying snakes doesn't prevent slither from capturing more creatures.

Critical Failure As failure, but the creature takes double damage and is restrained by a snake.

Heightened (+2) The persistent poison damage increases by 1d6 and snake HP increases by 6.

The target's senses are suddenly rewired in unexpected ways, causing them to process noises as bursts of color, smells as sounds, and so on. This has three effects, and the target must attempt a Will save.

  • Due to the distraction, the target must succeed at a @Check[flat|dc:5] each time it uses a concentrate action, or the action fails and is wasted.
  • The target's difficulty processing visual input makes all creatures and objects @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed} from it.

  • The creature has trouble moving, making it @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 3} and giving it a –10-foot status penalty to its Speeds.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is affected for 1 round.

Failure The target is affected for 1 minute.

Critical Failure As failure, and the target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 2} as it attempts to process the sensory shifts.

Heightened (9th) You can target up to five creatures.

If Ysondkhelir hits a creature with his Attack of Opportunity, he can teleport that creature to a dreamspace of his choosing.

@Localize[PF2E.NPC.Abilities.Glossary.AttackOfOpportunity]

One success Ysondkhelir's resistance to physical damage drops to 5. The south section of his window wall disappears.

Two successes No more crawling hands can spawn. The north section of Ysondkhelir's window wall disappears.

Three successes Ysondkhelir is no longer quickened. The remaining sections of his window wall disappear.

Four successes Ysondkhelir loses his Attack of Opportunity and his resistance to physical damage. He also reverts to his normal size and loses 15 feet reach on melee strikes. Dorianna is temporarily free of his mental influence, though he will eventually reassert control if left alive.
